answer.answer:
The study confirmed five challenging settings, each on a different scene. They are 1c45ce3a at +2 s and 1.0x (S22), 023b7fcc at -1.5 s and 1.25x (S1), 19f339ba at -1.5 s and 0.75x (S17), 096988dd at -1 s and 2x (S5), and 09a95ffa at -1 s and 1.25x (S7). Every kept run at each of these settings failed. S22 has the most repeats; the other four have only a few each, so their failure rates are only just shown to be above one half. However, only three of the five clearly show the policy's own mistakes:
- **S1 and S5:** the ego didn't brake enough for a slowing car ahead.
- **S17:** the ego braked hard for no reason, drifted left and hit a car beside it.

The other two mostly fail because of the replayed traffic, which doesn't react to the ego. At S22 the retimed cut-in car side-swipes an ego that is driving straight on its recorded path. At S7, a retimed car is already overlapping the ego when the policy takes over. Moving the cars earlier (-1 to -1.5 s) is common to most of the confirmed settings. But each scene was searched with only a few runs, so this is a pattern to check, not a map of where the policy fails.

findings.claim: 023b7fcc at -1.5 s and 1.25x fails reliably, and through the policy's fault. In two runs the ego held about 5.5 m/s and drove into the slower car ahead without braking. In the third it drifted out of its lane against a RIGHT command and side-swiped a neighbouring car. In one run, the car behind touched the ego's rear before the front hit.

096988dd at -1 s and 2x fails reliably because the ego braked too gently and too late for a slowing car ahead. That car was rendered as a heavy smear in every run, and in one run the triage put the failure down to rendering. So part of this case may come from the simulator. Nearby settings on this scene, at -1.5 s and 1.0x, and at -0.5 s and 1.5x, did not fail.

19f339ba at -1.5 s and 0.75x fails reliably, and through the policy's fault. After takeover the ego braked hard with a steady 18 m gap ahead, drifted left across the lane line and side-swiped a car in the left lane. At +0.5 s and 1.5x the scene did not fail.

1c45ce3a at +2 s and 1.0x fails at every repeat, but these are not policy failures. The ego drove straight, close to its recorded path, with no car ahead. Then the delayed cut-in car (track 14) came up from behind on the right and hit its side. The triage marks each run as not the policy's fault or unclear. Earlier timings on this scene (-2 s at 2x, -1.5 s at 1.25x, 0 s at 1.5x) did not fail.

09a95ffa at -1 s and 1.25x counts as confirmed, but it is mainly a replay artifact. A retimed faster car already overlapped the ego from behind at takeover and drove through it, setting the front-collision flag. In two runs the policy was not at fault. In the third the cause is unclear: the ego also steered left and hit a car in the next lane.

054b5901 at -0.5 s and 1.25x fails sometimes but was not confirmed. In the failures the ego ignored a RIGHT command, stayed in the far-left lane about 8 m off the recorded path, and left the road at the median. All of these failures are marked as possible artifacts because the ego was far from the recorded trajectory, but the triage judged the camera usable and the policy at fault.

No failure was found on 0cf6368d, 12855a41 or 0e899dd3 at any setting tried, which included early, fast retimings. But each setting there had only one or two runs, so this does not show those scenes are safe.

open: Whether S22 and S7 are real policy failures. Those failures come from replayed cars that don't react to the ego. Re-running them with reactive traffic, or retiming only the cut-in car on 09a95ffa, would tell.
The failure rates at S1, S5, S7 and S17 are only just above one half. More repeats at each would pin them down.
Whether S5 depends on the smeared rendering of the car ahead. Repeats with a check for rendering artifacts would settle it.

Whether 054b5901 at -0.5 s and 1.25x (S2) is a real off-road case. Its failures are marked as possible artifacts and its rate is unsettled; more repeats with the trajectory artifact checked would settle it. If it holds, it could replace S7 or S22 as a policy-caused case.
Whether 0cf6368d, 12855a41 and 0e899dd3 can be broken at all. Each setting tried there had only one or two runs; a denser search near their closest approaches (e.g. S13, S15, S11) would tell.
Near misses were not ranked, and the study cannot tell apart cases where the ego merges from cases where another car cuts in.
